audits.title: Audit of total parenteral nutrition in an adult surgical intensive care.
audits.standard: Stanford University Hospital TPN indications; caloric requirements by Harris-Benedict and 30 to 35 kcal/kg/day
audits.setting: Adult surgical intensive care unit, Singapore General Hospital

cycle1.result: Indications comparable with Stanford criteria; 64.3% overfed; 50% excessive non-protein calorie-to-nitrogen ratio; 98% and 81% below recommended amino acid and glucose; 58% adequate lipids

audits.other_findings: 50 patients received TPN, 4 records unavailable; 52.2% survived to discharge; hyperglycaemia and line sepsis increased with TPN duration.
audits.citation: Tay SM, Ip-Yam PC, Lim BL, Chan YW. Audit of total parenteral nutrition in an adult surgical intensive care. Ann Acad Med Singap. 2002;31(4):487-492. doi:10.47102/annals-acadmedsg.v31n4p487. PMID: 12161885.

audits.title: An Audit of the Use of Total Parenteral Nutrition: Are We Using It Correctly?
audits.standard: NICE (2017) and NCEPOD (2010) standards for parenteral nutrition, plus local guidelines
audits.setting: General surgery inpatients (ICU excluded); affiliations include Stepping Hill, Pilgrim and George Eliot hospitals

cycle1.result: Three previous audit cycles (results not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: Indication documented 100%; other feeding routes excluded 13 (81.25%); MUST used 100%; 15 (93.75%) no weight/BMI documented at end of TPN; 5 (31.25%) emergency TPN started out of hours; all prescribed adequately.

audits.other_findings: Across four cycles dietitian review (p = 0.002) and correct prescription (p < 0.001) improved significantly, but weight/BMI documentation declined (p = 0.008).
audits.citation: Kumar A, Taggarsi M, Rai S. An Audit of the Use of Total Parenteral Nutrition: Are We Using It Correctly?. Cureus. 2026;18(1):e102333. doi:10.7759/cureus.102333. PMID: 41755986.

audits.title: Audit of Parenteral Nutrition Use in Surgical Patients: Compliance With the 2017 American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition Guidelines.
audits.setting: Department of General Surgery, Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research

cycle1.result: CVC tip confirmed radiologically in 40/47 and refeeding risk assessed in 43/47; blood glucose monitoring less frequent than recommended

audits.other_findings: Hyponatraemia and hypomagnesaemia 78.72%; catheter-related bloodstream infection in 11 patients.
audits.citation: Anvesh T, Elamurugan TP, Sistla SC. Audit of Parenteral Nutrition Use in Surgical Patients: Compliance With the 2017 American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition Guidelines. Cureus. 2026;18(8):e114218. doi:10.7759/cureus.114218. PMID: 42713294.

audits.title: Audit of parenteral nutrition use in Guernsey.
audits.standard: NICE and local Guernsey guidelines on initiation, monitoring and cessation of parenteral nutrition

cycle1.result: PN initiated appropriately; re-feeding risk assessed routinely except for two weekend admissions; five patients not given appropriate IV Pabrinex; only 13 had accurate daily fluid-balance charts; 11 of 17 planned cessations weaned appropriately.

audits.other_findings: The main problem was PN started at or just before the weekend; two patients were readmitted with feeding problems within 28 days.
audits.citation: Harbottle L, Brache E, Clarke J. Audit of parenteral nutrition use in Guernsey. Int J Pharm Pract. 2009;17(5):293-298. doi:10.1211/ijpp.17.05.0006. PMID: 20214271.

audits.title: Adult parenteral nutrition in the North of England: a region-wide audit.
audits.standard: NCEPOD report 'A Mixed Bag' recommendations on parenteral nutrition
audits.setting: All 10 secondary care hospitals in the Northern Nutrition Network region, North of England

cycle1.result: 30-day mortality 8%; metabolic complications 34% (13% avoidable); catheter sepsis 1.5 per 1000 PN days; refeeding risk identified in 75%; treatment goal documented 39%, PN constitution reviewed 38%, regular weighing 56%, line-tip position documented 52%.

audits.other_findings: Nutrition team input improved assessment before PN and review once established; documentation remained suboptimal.
audits.citation: Dyson JK, Thompson N, Northern Nutrition Network. Adult parenteral nutrition in the North of England: a region-wide audit. BMJ Open. 2017;7(1):e012663. doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2016-012663. PMID: 28073792.
